description: The app's chat key (rc4-32): bound at POST /v1/device/token (worker.schema.json $defs/chat_key_bind) by bind_signature over "leanctx.cloud.chat_key_bind.v1\n" followed by canonical_json({alg, instance_public_key (the request's string), key_id, public_key, scope: "person_publish.v1"}); it then signs the person's own posts only ("leanctx.cloud.person_publish.v1\n" followed by canonical_json): the relay place.publish (frame without presence_signature, plus instance_id) and the engine-token chat routes (body without presence_signature, plus instance_id, t "chat.message" with channel_id, or t "chat.dm"; the body carries client_msg_id, a UUID v4; the same signed post again answers the first post for as long as it exists, the same client_msg_id with another signed body is refused). The Cloud refuses it on any other check (refused_on_optin). A chat_key member set to null is refused (refused_null_chat_key), never read as absent. Test keys only: chat key ed25519 seed = sha256("leanctx-cloud test chat key: rc4-32"); instance_public_key = standard base64 of the ed25519 public key of seed sha256("leanctx-cloud test instance key: rc4-32"). Cases engine_*: chat key seed = sha256("leanctx test chat key: rc4-32"), the engine's test key. engine_bind is the engine's bind vector (p5 !622 chat_key.rs, instance_public_key its fixed test string), cross-checked byte for byte; engine_chat_dm and engine_relay_person_publish are p37's vectors in the shapes the engine sends (a DM body with member UUIDs; the whole person place.publish frame with schema and type), signed with that key, for the engine to pin (pending in p5 !622). Each carries its own seed, public_key, signing_input and signature.

cases.name: refused_null_chat_key
cases.expect: 400 invalid_field field chat_key: a present chat_key is an object (chat_key_bind); leave the member out to bind no chat key, null is never read as absent
